μετεσχήκαμεν δὲ καὶ τῆς ἁγίας αὐτοῦ σαρκὸς, ἡγιάσμεθά τε διττῶς· καὶ κατῴκηκεν 264
ἐν ἡμῖν ὡς ζωὴ καὶ ζωοποιὸς, ἵνα τὸν τοῖς μέλεσιν ἡμῶν ἐπισκήψαντα θάνατον
καταργήσῃ δι' ἑαυτοῦ· καὶ τοῦτο ἡμᾶς ἀπαλλάσσει φθορᾶς καὶ τῶν τοῦ θανάτου βρόχων
καὶ ἀμείνους ποιεῖ παθῶν σαρκικῶν. καὶ δεχόμεθα τὴν ἄζυμον ἐν ἑαυτοῖς διδασκαλίαν
τῶν θείων λογίων τὴν τρέφουσαν τὸ ἡγεμονικὸν, καὶ συζῶμεν Χριστῷ, δῆλον δὲ ὅτι
πνευματικῶς, περιγενόμενοι τῶν τῆς σαρκὸς παθῶν. εἰ τοίνυν αὐτός ἐστιν "ἡ κεφαλὴ
τοῦ σώματος τῆς ἐκκλησίας," ἡμεῖς ἄρα ἐσμὲν οἱ καθ' ἕκαστα μέλη· ὅταν οὖν εἰς
ἀτόπους ἡδονὰς καταπίπτωμεν, τότε δὴ τότε πλημμελήσομεν εἰς αὐτὸν, οὗ καὶ
γεγόναμεν μέλη· πόρνοις γὰρ ὥσπερ τὰ αὐτοῦ χαριούμεθα· τὰ μέλη αὐτοῦ μολύνονται
τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ καὶ πόρνης ποιοῦνται μέλη. ὥσπερ γὰρ ὁ γυναικὶ κολλώμενος ἓν πρὸς αὐτὴν
ἔσται σῶμα, οὕτως καὶ ὁ Θεῷ συνδεσμούμενος νοητῶς ἒν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἔσται πνεῦμα·
γεγόναμεν γὰρ "θείας κοινωνοὶ φύσεως," συνήφθημέν τε καὶ ἡγιάσμεθα διὰ τοῦ
Πνεύματος ἐν Χριστῷ.

ΤΟΥ ΑΥΤΟΥ ΚΥΡΙΛΛΟΥ ΕΚ ΤΟΥ Γ ΤΟΜΟΥ ΤΗΣ ΠΡΟΣ ΚΟΡΙΝΘΙΟΥΣ.
Πᾶν ἁμάρτημα ὃ ἐὰν ποιήσῃ ἄνθρωπος, ἐκτὸς τοῦ σώματός ἐστιν, ὁ δὲ πορνεύων
εἰς τὸ ἴδιον σῶμα ἁμαρτάνει. ΦΑΙΗ τις ἄν Ὁ φονευτὴς, εἰπέ μοι, τίνα δὴ τρόπον
ἐνεργήσει τὸν φόνον; ἆρ' οὐ δι' αἵματος; εἰ δὲ δή τις ἕλοιτο φιλοψογεῖν ἑτέρους, οὐ διὰ
γλώττης ἐστὶ τοιοῦτος; εἶτα ποῖον ἔσται τῶν πλημμελημάτων ὃ δρῶτο ἂν, οὐχὶ διὰ τοῦ
σώματος; ψευδοέπης οὖν ἆρα λοιπὸν ὁ πνευματοφόρος ἀναφανεῖταί που; μὴ γένοιτο·
λαλεῖ γὰρ ἐν Χριστῷ, Χριστὸς δέ ἐστιν ἡ ἀλήθεια· ἔσται δὴ οὖν ἀληθής. εἰ τῇδέ πη. τὸ
χρῆμα διασκεπτόμεθα, εἴ τις ἕλοιτο τυχὸν σκαιὸς εἶναι τοὺς τρόπους, εἰς ἑτέρους που
πάντως ἔσται τοιοῦτος καὶ οὐκ εἰς ἑαυτόν. ἀποκτενεῖ γὰρ ὁ φονευτὴς, οὐχ ἑαυτὸν, ἀλλ'
ἑτέρους, ὑβρίσει δὲ καὶ ὁ λοίδορος οὐχ ἑαυτὸν, ἀλλ' ἑτέρους, ἀδικήσει δὲ καὶ ὁ
πλεονέκτης οὐχ ἑαυτὸν ἀλλ' ἐφ' ἑτέρους, καὶ ἐφ' ἑκάστῳ τῶν ἐκτόπων τινὰ τῶν
δρωμένων τοιαύτην εὑρήσεις ὁδόν. οὐκοῦν κατὰ τόνδε τὸν τρόπον Πᾶν ἁμάρτημα
ἐκτὸς τοῦ σώματός ἐστιν, ὁ δὲ πορνεύων εἰς τὸ ἴδιον σῶμα ἁμαρτάνει. ἁλώσεται γὰρ
ἀδικῶν αὐτὸ τὸ ἴδιον σῶμα, 266 καὶ τίνα τρόπον, ἐρῶ. τὰ μέλη τοῦ σώματος ἡμῶν διὰ
μὲν τῆς ἁγνείας Χριστοῦ μέλη μεμενηκότα, μεθέξουσι πάντως τῆς παρ' αὐτοῦ ζωῆς τε
καὶ δόξης· "μετασχηματίσει γὰρ τὸ "σῶμα τῆς ταπεινώσεως ἡμῶν σύμμορφον τῷ
σώματι τῆς "δόξης αὐτοῦ·" εἰ δὲ δὴ γένοιτο πόρνης μέλη, πῶς ἂν λάβοι τὸν
μετασχηματισμὸν καὶ τὴν τῆς πρὸς αὐτὸν συμμορφίας λαμπρότητα νοητήν;
ἐγηγερμένων γὰρ τῶν ἀπὸ γῆς σωμάτων κατὰ τὸν τῆς ἀναστάσεως καιρόν
"Ἐκλάμψουσι μὲν οἱ "δίκαιοι ὡς ὁ ἥλιος," οἱ δὲ ἀσεβεῖς τε καὶ βέβηλοι καὶ βεβιωκότες
ἐκτόπως, ἐγερθήσονται μὲν, οὐ μὴν ἔτι καὶ τὴν εὐκλεᾶ διαβιώσονται ζωὴν, ἀμέτοχοι δὲ
μένουσι καὶ δόξης· ἀναστήσονται γὰρ οὐκ "ἐν κρίσει οὔτε μὴν ἐν βουλῇ "δικαίων," ἀλλ'
ἐπὶ ποινῇ καὶ δίκῃ, κατοιχήσονται γὰρ εἰς τὸ σκότος τὸ ἐξώτερον· πῶς γὰρ ἐν δόξῃ τὸ
κολαζόμενον; προσεπάγει δέ τι καὶ ἕτερον, οὐκ ἀνικάνως ἔχον ἀναπεῖσαι μισεῖν τὴν
ἐπάρατον τοῦ σώματος ἡδονήν.
Ἐπειδὴ καὶ ὁ φονεύων καὶ ἀτιμάζων καὶ λοιδορῶν, εἰ καὶ σώματι ποιεῖ τὴν
ἁμαρτίαν, ἀλλ' ὅμως εἰς ἑτέρους αὐτὸ πράττει, τούτων τῶν τρόπων λέγεται Πᾶν
ἁμάρτημα ἐκτὸς τοῦ σώματος, ὁ δὲ πορνεύων αὐτὸ τὸ ἴδιον ἀδικεῖ σῶμα· τὰ σώματα
ἡμῶν δι' ἁγνείας μένουσι μέλη Χριστοῦ, καὶ μεταλαμβάνουσι τῆς παρ' αὐτοῦ ζωῆς καὶ

δόξης· ἐὰν δὲ μολυνθῇ, στερεῖται τῆς τοιαύτης δόξης. Οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι τὸ σῶμα ὑμῶν
ναὸς τοῦ ἐν ὑμῖν Ἁγίου Πνεύματος. Κατῴκηκε γὰρ ἐν ἡμῖν τὸ τῆς "υἱοθεσίας Πνεῦμα,"
pass_a_gloss: [block opens mid-sentence; preceding block: 'we have him in ourselves perceptibly (αἰσθητῶς)'] …and intelligibly/spiritually (νοητῶς). For he dwells (κατοικέω) in our hearts (καρδία) through the Spirit (Πνεῦμα), and we have also partaken (μετέχω, pf.) of his holy flesh (σάρξ), and we have been sanctified (ἁγιάζω, pf. pass.) doubly (διττῶς); and he has dwelt (κατοικέω, pf.) in us as life (ζωή) and life-giving (ζωοποιός), so that he might abolish (καταργέω) through himself the death (θάνατος) that had fallen upon (ἐπισκήπτω) our members (μέλος); and this frees (ἀπαλλάσσω) us from corruption (φθορά) and the nooses (βρόχος) of death and makes us better (ἀμείνων) than fleshly passions (πάθος σαρκικόν). And we receive (δέχομαι) in ourselves the unleavened (ἄζυμος) teaching (διδασκαλία) of the divine oracles (λόγιον) which nourishes (τρέφω) the ruling part (ἡγεμονικόν), and we live with (συζάω) Christ, clearly (δῆλον) spiritually (πνευματικῶς), having prevailed over (περιγίνομαι) the passions of the flesh. If then he is 'the head (κεφαλή) of the body (σῶμα) of the church (ἐκκλησία)', we then are the members severally (καθ' ἕκαστα). Whenever therefore we fall down (καταπίπτω) into out-of-place (ἄτοπος) pleasures (ἡδονή), then indeed then we shall offend (πλημμελέω, fut.) against him of whom we have become members; for to fornicators (πόρνος, masc. dat. pl.) as it were we shall make a present of (χαρίζομαι, fut.) the things that are his; his members are defiled (μολύνω) by sin (ἁμαρτία) and are made members of a harlot (πόρνη). For as the one cleaving (κολλάω) to a woman will be one body with her, so also the one bound together (συνδεσμέω) with God intelligibly (νοητῶς) will be one spirit (πνεῦμα) with him; for we have become 'sharers (κοινωνός) of divine nature (φύσις)', and we were joined (συνάπτω, aor. pass.) and have been sanctified through the Spirit in Christ. [Heading:] Of the same Cyril, from the third tome (τόμος) of the [work] to the Corinthians. [Lemma:] Every sin (ἁμάρτημα) whatever a man does is outside (ἐκτός) the body; but the one committing fornication (πορνεύω) sins (ἁμαρτάνω) into his own (ἴδιος) body. Someone might say: The murderer (φονευτής), tell me, in what way will he work (ἐνεργέω) the murder (φόνος)? Is it not through blood (αἷμα)? And if someone should choose (αἱρέομαι) to love finding fault (φιλοψογέω) with others, is he not such through the tongue (γλῶττα)? Then which of the offences (πλημμέλημα) will there be that might be done not through the body? Will the Spirit-bearer (πνευματοφόρος) then after all appear (ἀναφαίνομαι) somewhere false-speaking (ψευδοεπής)? May it not be (μὴ γένοιτο); for he speaks (λαλέω) in Christ, and Christ is the truth (ἀλήθεια); he will therefore be true (ἀληθής). If in this way we examine (διασκέπτομαι) the matter (χρῆμα): if someone should perhaps choose to be perverse (σκαιός) in his ways (τρόπος), he will be such surely toward others and not toward himself. For the murderer will kill (ἀποκτείνω) not himself but others; and the reviler (λοίδορος) will insult (ὑβρίζω) not himself but others; and the greedy man (πλεονέκτης) will wrong (ἀδικέω) not himself but others; and in each of the outrageous (ἔκτοπος) things done you will find some such road (ὁδός). Therefore in this way every sin is outside the body, but the fornicator sins into his own body. For he will be caught (ἁλίσκομαι, fut.) wronging his very own body, and in what way, I will say. The members of our body, through purity (ἁγνεία) having remained (μένω, pf. ptc.) members of Christ, will surely partake (μετέχω, fut.) of the life and glory (δόξα) from him; 'for he will transform (μετασχηματίζω) the body of our lowliness (ταπείνωσις) conformed (σύμμορφος) to the body of his glory'; but if they should become members of a harlot, how could it receive the transformation (μετασχηματισμός) and the intelligible (νοητός) brightness (λαμπρότης) of conformity (συμμορφία) to him? For the bodies from earth having been raised (ἐγείρω) at the time of the resurrection (ἀνάστασις), 'the righteous (δίκαιος) will shine forth (ἐκλάμπω) as the sun'; but the impious (ἀσεβής) and profane (βέβηλος) and those having lived outrageously will be raised, yet not also live through (διαβιόω) the glorious (εὐκλεής) life, but remain without share (ἀμέτοχος) of glory too; for they will rise (ἀνίστημι) not 'in judgment (κρίσις) nor in the council (βουλή) of the righteous', but for penalty (ποινή) and punishment (δίκη), for they will go down (κατοίχομαι) into the outer darkness (σκότος ἐξώτερον); for how [is] the one punished (κολάζω) in glory? And he adds (προσεπάγω) something else too, not incapable of persuading (ἀναπείθω) [us] to hate (μισέω) the accursed (ἐπάρατος) pleasure of the body. [Second fragment:] Since both the one murdering and dishonoring (ἀτιμάζω) and reviling (λοιδορέω), even if he does the sin with the body, nevertheless does it into others, in these ways it is said 'Every sin is outside the body', but the fornicator wrongs his very own body; our bodies through purity remain members of Christ and partake of the life and glory from him; but if it be defiled, it is deprived (στερέω) of such glory. [Lemma:] Do you not know that your body is a temple (ναός) of the Holy Spirit in you. For the 'Spirit of adoption (υἱοθεσία)' has dwelt in us, [continues in u02-rem-close]
pass_b_english: …and in a spiritual way. For he dwells in our hearts through the Spirit (compare Ephesians 3:17), and we have also shared in his holy flesh; so we have been made holy in two ways. He has come to dwell in us as life and as the giver of life, so that through himself he might abolish the death that had fallen upon our members. This frees us from corruption and from the snares of death, and raises us above the passions of the flesh. We also receive within ourselves the unleavened teaching of the divine oracles (compare 1 Corinthians 5:8), which nourishes the ruling part of the soul, and we live together with Christ, spiritually of course, having overcome the passions of the flesh.

If, then, he is “the head of the body, the church” (Colossians 1:18), we are its members, each one in particular. So whenever we fall into unseemly pleasures, then, precisely then, we will sin against him whose members we have become. For we will be, as it were, handing over what is his to fornicators: his members are defiled by sin and are made members of a prostitute (1 Corinthians 6:15). For just as the man who is joined to a woman will be one body with her, so also the one who is bound to God spiritually will be one spirit with him (1 Corinthians 6:16–17). For we have become “partakers of the divine nature” (2 Peter 1:4), and we have been joined to him and made holy through the Spirit in Christ.
From the third book on the Letter to the Corinthians, by the same Cyril.
“Every sin that a person commits is outside the body, but the one who commits fornication sins against his own body” (1 Corinthians 6:18).

Someone might say: “Tell me, how will the murderer carry out his murder? Is it not by bloodshed? And if someone chooses to find fault with others, is it not with his tongue that he is such a man? What offense, then, could be committed other than through the body? Will the bearer of the Spirit, then, turn out after all to have spoken falsely?” By no means! For he speaks in Christ (compare 2 Corinthians 2:17), and Christ is the truth (John 14:6); so he will be truthful.

Suppose we look into the matter this way: if someone happens to choose to be perverse in his ways, he will surely be so toward others and not toward himself. The murderer will kill not himself but others; the reviler will insult not himself but others; the greedy man will wrong not himself but others; and in each outrageous deed that is done you will find the same course. In this sense, then, “every sin is outside the body, but the one who commits fornication sins against his own body.” For he will be caught wronging his very own body, and I will say in what way.

The members of our body, if through purity they have remained members of Christ, will surely share in the life and glory that come from him; for “he will transform the body of our lowliness to be conformed to the body of his glory” (Philippians 3:21). But if they should become members of a prostitute, how could they receive that transformation and the spiritual splendor of being conformed to him? For when earthly bodies have been raised at the time of the resurrection, “the righteous will shine like the sun” (Matthew 13:43). The ungodly, the profane, and those who have lived outrageously will indeed be raised, yet they will not go on to live the glorious life; they remain without any share in glory. For they will rise not “in judgment, nor in the council of the righteous” (Psalm 1:5), but for penalty and punishment, for they will go down into the outer darkness (compare Matthew 25:30). For how can what is being punished be in glory? And he adds something more, which has no small power to persuade us to hate the accursed pleasure of the body.

The one who murders, the one who dishonors, and the one who reviles commit the sin with the body, yet they do it against others. In this sense it is said, “Every sin is outside the body,” but the one who commits fornication wrongs his very own body. Through purity our bodies remain members of Christ and share in the life and glory that come from him; but if the body is defiled, it is deprived of that glory.
“Do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you?” (1 Corinthians 6:19). For “the Spirit of adoption” (Romans 8:15) has come to dwell in us…

choices.why: Cyril then explains the two ways.

choices.english: raises us above the passions of the flesh
rejected: makes us better than the passions
choices.why: The sense is superiority over the passions.
The verb of departing to the underworld.

bible_refs.note: κατοικεῖ … ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ἡμῶν echoes κατοικῆσαι τὸν Χριστὸν … ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν; Cyril has 'through the Spirit' where Paul has 'through faith', so marked 'compare'.
τὴν ἄζυμον … διδασκαλίαν picks up the 'unleavened bread of sincerity and truth' (ἐν ἀζύμοις εἰλικρινείας καὶ ἀληθείας) of the chapter Cyril has just expounded.
αὐτός ἐστιν ἡ κεφαλὴ τοῦ σώματος τῆς ἐκκλησίας matches Colossians 1:18 word for word.
πόρνης ποιοῦνται μέλη recalls ἄρας οὖν τὰ μέλη τοῦ Χριστοῦ ποιήσω πόρνης μέλη;

ὁ γυναικὶ κολλώμενος ἓν … σῶμα … ὁ Θεῷ συνδεσμούμενος … ἓν … πνεῦμα paraphrases 6:16 (ὁ κολλώμενος τῇ πόρνῃ ἓν σῶμά ἐστιν) and 6:17 (ὁ δὲ κολλώμενος τῷ κυρίῳ ἓν πνεῦμά ἐστιν); Cyril has 'woman' and 'God'.
θείας κοινωνοὶ φύσεως = 2 Peter 1:4 (γένησθε θείας κοινωνοὶ φύσεως).
Lemma, quoted in full: πᾶν ἁμάρτημα ὃ ἐὰν ποιήσῃ ἄνθρωπος ἐκτὸς τοῦ σώματός ἐστιν· ὁ δὲ πορνεύων εἰς τὸ ἴδιον σῶμα ἁμαρτάνει. Repeated in short form twice later in the block.
λαλεῖ γὰρ ἐν Χριστῷ echoes ἐν Χριστῷ λαλοῦμεν (2 Corinthians 2:17; also 12:19).
Χριστὸς δέ ἐστιν ἡ ἀλήθεια: Christ's own saying ἐγώ εἰμι … ἡ ἀλήθεια.
μετασχηματίσει τὸ σῶμα τῆς ταπεινώσεως ἡμῶν σύμμορφον τῷ σώματι τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ matches Philippians 3:21.
ἐκλάμψουσιν οἱ δίκαιοι ὡς ὁ ἥλιος; Cyril adds μέν and puts the verb first.
LXX Psalm 1:5 οὐκ ἀναστήσονται ἀσεβεῖς ἐν κρίσει οὐδὲ ἁμαρτωλοὶ ἐν βουλῇ δικαίων; Psalm 1 has the same number in LXX and Hebrew.
εἰς τὸ σκότος τὸ ἐξώτερον is the Gospel phrase of Matthew 8:12; 22:13; 25:30; cited once with 'compare' since no single verse is quoted.
Lemma: οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι τὸ σῶμα ὑμῶν ναὸς τοῦ ἐν ὑμῖν ἁγίου πνεύματός ἐστιν; the source omits ἐστιν and ends with a full stop; rendered as Paul's question.
τὸ τῆς υἱοθεσίας Πνεῦμα begins the citation of Romans 8:15 that finishes in u02-rem-close (ἐν ᾧ κράζομεν Ἀββᾶ ὁ πατήρ).
